posts.author: andyl
posts.content_md:
[http://picasaweb.google.com/andylesniak ... imateHolos](http://picasaweb.google.com/andylesniak/FirstUltimateHolos)

I haven't posted in a while, have been working way toooo much..

but just got a sample of some ultimate, here is the first shot

using a C315 @ running @ 30mw (turned it down) 

spread to just over 4x5, 1 sec exposure... I'm thinking it might be a little over exposed. 

other info. develop 6min ultimate developer, bleach 2min.

gotta say if it wasn't for the haze/fog it's as bright as a dcg. 

another note... tried developer/bleach on vrp-m, results are close.

vrp-m is a dark red which blocks majority of the beam, resulting in dim hologram. Split beam with a close 1:1 ratio is almost as bright as the ultimate. 

config. Denisyuk, plate resting on object.[/img]

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: very nice! how well does it replay in the green laser ?this hologram could make a good reflection master.

posts.author: andyl
posts.content_md:
replay in laser is fantastic, just as if the object was there. I also made

a vrp-m reflection raising the plate about 6 inches above the object to

get a almost 1:1 ratio, in regular light/sunlight it's a little fuzzzy, but

in laser light 100% sharp. 

Anyone else use ultimate? is the fogging due to overexposure?

I believe I read (on ultimate's web site) that is the cause..

posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.content_md:
I always use Ultimate and the most off the holograms are great.

If the plate looks milky then the expose time is to long try a shorter expose time.

I made this week 6 ultimates and they look great.
